sources.title: Log sources
sources.description: Devices that send syslog to the box {{ip}}.
sources.descriptionInfo: The box only accepts logs from the IPs declared here.
sources.caption: Log sources currently received
sources.silentHint: No new line for over 1 hour: check power, network and firewall port {{port}}.
sources.neverHint: Save the settings on the device, wait 1 to 2 minutes, then press Refresh.
sources.viaSnmp: found by the address its SNMP is read from
sources.matchesSeveral: More than one device has this address:
sources.emptyBody: Add the first device or program that sends logs.
sources.emptyBodyInfo: Such as a firewall, NAS, Windows server or web server. Vedette then shows the exact settings to enter on it.
sources.descriptionNoIp: Box address unknown: add your LAN range first (Settings, Scanning, Safety).
sources.noIpReason: The box takes its address from your LAN range.
sources.noIpLink: Add the LAN range in Settings, Scanning, Safety
sources.noIpAskAdmin: Ask an administrator to add the LAN range in Settings, Scanning, Safety.
sources.descriptionNoIpInfo: Devices that send syslog to the box. The box only accepts logs from the IPs declared here.
sources.descriptionNoIpLan: Point devices at the address of the machine that runs Vedette.
sources.descriptionNoIpLanInfo: Devices that send syslog to the box. The box cannot see its own address in your LAN range {{lan}}, as when it runs in a container: point devices at the address of the machine that runs Vedette, the one you open this page on. The box only accepts logs from the IPs declared here.

unknown.title: Syslog from an address that is not a source
unknown.notSource: {{ip}} sends syslog over {{proto}}, but no source has this IP, so the box drops its lines ({{times}}, last {{when}}).
unknown.notSourceInfo: Add it as a source, or change the sender IP of the source you meant.
unknown.otherProto: {{ip}} sends syslog over {{proto}}, but {{name}} is declared with {{declared}}, so the box drops its lines ({{times}}, last {{when}}).
unknown.otherProtoInfo: Make the protocol of the source and of the device the same.
unknown.container: On a container install, syslog sent from the machine that runs Vedette arrives from the containers' network gateway (often 172.17.0.1 or 172.18.0.1), not from the machine's own address: declare that address for such a source.
unknown.memory: Counted since the syslog listener last started; the 10 most recent addresses are shown.
unknown.forged: UDP sender addresses can be forged: check it is your device first.
unknown.forgedInfo: The sender address of a UDP datagram can be forged: check that the address is a device of yours before you add it.

form.addDescInfo: The next step shows the exact settings to enter on that device.
form.name: Name
form.nameHintInfo: Letters without accents, digits, dashes, dots and underscores, starting with a letter or digit.
form.ipHint: The box only accepts logs from this IP. Example: 192.168.10.1.

protoHint.udp: Keeps this device's lines over UDP or TCP.
protoHint.tcp: Keeps only TCP from this device.
protoHint.tls: The box keeps only TLS from this device, on port 6514.

protoInfo.udp: The box listens on UDP and TCP and keeps this device's lines from either.
protoInfo.tcp: The box listens on UDP and TCP but keeps only TCP from this device: UDP is easy to forge.

form.added: Log source added. Apply the setup on the device to start receiving.
form.deleteBody: The box stops accepting logs from this IP.
form.deleteBodyInfo: Logs already received are kept until the retention period ends. The device configuration is not removed.
form.noMatch: Nothing matches "{{q}}". Try another word, or choose Other device (standard syslog).
form.certHint: Optional: the device certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint.
form.certHintInfo: Leave empty to accept the device by its IP address alone. To also require the device to present its own certificate, paste that certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint (64 hexadecimal characters; colons and spaces are fine).
form.certBad: A SHA-256 fingerprint is 64 hexadecimal characters, like AB:CD:... or abcd...

config.title: Set up {{name}} to send logs to the box
config.target: The box receives at {{ip}}, port {{port}}/{{proto}}. It only accepts logs from {{sender}}.
config.verify: After saving on the device, wait 1 to 2 minutes and press Refresh: the status changes to Receiving.
config.reads: What Vedette reads from this source
config.noIp: The box address is not known yet. Add your LAN range first.
config.noIpInfo: Add it under Settings, Scanning, Safety. Until then the settings below show {{placeholder}} where the box address goes.
config.noIpLan: Use the address of the machine that runs Vedette.
config.noIpLanInfo: The box cannot see its own address in your LAN range {{lan}}, as when it runs in a container. Use the address of the machine that runs Vedette, the one you open this page on: the settings below show {{placeholder}} where it goes.
config.tlsTrust: Over TLS the device must trust the box certificate.
config.tlsTrustInfo: Download the box certificate shown under the log sources and import it on the device. The box accepts logs from this device by its IP address.
config.tlsTrustPinned: Over TLS the device must trust the box certificate and present its own.
config.tlsTrustPinnedInfo: Download the box certificate shown under the log sources and import it on the device. The device must present the client certificate whose fingerprint you entered for this source: the box closes any other connection.

bad.title: Connections to bad IPs or domains
bad.description: Devices that reached, or tried to reach, an address on a threat feed.
bad.descriptionInfo: The address is on a threat feed stored on the box. The box sees this in metadata from a SPAN or mirror port (DNS queries, TLS server names, HTTP host names, flows) or in syslog from a firewall, DNS server or proxy.
bad.descriptionNoSpan: Devices that reached, or tried to reach, an address on a threat feed.
bad.descriptionNoSpanInfo: The address is on a threat feed stored on the box. The box sees this in syslog from a firewall, DNS server or proxy.
bad.caption: Connections to bad IPs or domains
bad.listedAsHint: The feed lists this name with all of its subdomains, so the name the device asked for is a bad destination too.
bad.blockedHint: The device that sent this log blocked the connection: the line records an attempt. A device that tries to reach a listed address may still be infected.
bad.empty: None of your devices connected to a listed bad address in the last 24 hours.
bad.empty7d: None of your devices connected to a listed bad address in the last 7 days.
bad.emptyFeedsOff: The Feeds module is off, so no connection can be matched.
bad.feedsOffReason: Turn on Feeds to match connections against threat feeds.
bad.emptyNoIoc: No switched-on threat feed lists any IP address or domain yet, so no connection can be matched.
bad.emptyNoIocAction: Switch on an IOC feed under Feeds, or wait for its first download.
bad.note: SPAN rows come from metadata only: the box keeps names, addresses and counts, never the content of traffic. Set up a mirror port in Settings → Box network (on a container-only install, under Sensor in Devices → Sensor and agents).
bad.noteKept: SPAN rows come from metadata only: the box keeps names, addresses and counts, never the content of traffic.

new.title: New compared with {{days}} days ago
new.description: Log types never seen before from the same source.
new.descriptionInfo: Grouped by type rather than listed line by line.
new.caption: New log types
new.empty: No new log types compared with {{days}} days ago.
new.emptyLearning: No new log types yet. The box is still learning: {{n}} of {{days}} days so far.

spikes.title: Spikes
spikes.description: Log types that appear far more often than the {{days}}-day average.
spikes.caption: Log types with a spike
spikes.empty: No log type is unusually high.

none.title: No logs to analyse yet
none.body: Add a log source and paste its configuration into the device.
none.bodyInfo: The digest needs a few days of logs to know what normal looks like. After configuring the device, come back in 1 to 2 minutes.

events.title: Search events
events.description: Search the logs stored on the box.
events.caption: Log events
events.capped: Only the newest 200 lines are shown. Narrow the time range or add a keyword.
events.found_one: 1 matching line in this time range.
events.found_other: {{count}} matching lines in this time range.
events.partial_one: 1 matching line found so far, searched back to {{time}}. Older lines are not searched yet.
events.partial_other: {{count}} matching lines found so far, searched back to {{time}}. Older lines are not searched yet.
events.searchOlderFailed: The search could not continue. Try again.
events.empty: No matching line. Try a longer time range or remove the keyword.
events.emptyNone: No log line in this range yet.
events.emptyNoneInfo: If you just configured the device, wait 1 to 2 minutes and press Refresh in the Log sources section.

retention.title: Log retention
retention.description: Older logs are deleted automatically. {{days}} days take about {{mb}} MB now.
retention.descriptionNone: Older logs are deleted automatically. No lines arrive now, so no size estimate yet.
retention.label: Keep logs for
retention.shortenBody: Log lines older than {{n}} days will be deleted at the next cleanup (within about an hour) and cannot be restored.

siem.title: Forward to a SIEM
siem.description: Copies events to your SIEM (Wazuh, Graylog, Splunk, Elastic).
siem.descriptionInfo: Data only goes to the destination you enter here; switching it off stops it immediately.
siem.urlHint: The box sends a POST with a JSON body to this address.
siem.secretHintInfo: Each request then carries X-Vedette-Timestamp (Unix seconds) and X-Vedette-Signature (sha256=<hex>): HMAC-SHA256 with this key over the timestamp, a dot and the raw body.
siem.secretSaved: Saved, ending in {{last4}}. Leave empty to keep it.
siem.secretLost: The saved key was not restored with the backup. Enter it again (or press Generate random and put the new key in your SIEM), then save.
siem.lostTitle: Forwarding is stopped: the saved signing key was not restored
siem.lostBody: The backup was restored without its decryption key, or the box key changed. Nothing is sent to the SIEM until you enter the signing key again below and save.
siem.lostKeyTitle: The saved signing key was not restored
siem.lostKeyBody: The backup was restored without its decryption key, or the box key changed. Enter the signing key again below before the JSON webhook can send.

event.bad_conn: Connections to bad IPs or domains

siem.noHoneypot: Not on this install: the honeypot needs the appliance install.
siem.sample: Sample of one record that will be sent
siem.testWaiting: Sending a test record to your SIEM… this can take up to 30 seconds.
siem.adminOnly: Only administrators can change this setting.
siem.cefHint: CEF: 7 header fields separated by |, then key=value pairs.

boxCert.title: Box certificate for syslog over TLS
boxCert.subject: Subject
boxCert.box_ca: Import the box's own certificate authority (port {{port}}) on devices as trusted. Do not pin the server certificate.
boxCert.box_caInfo: The box CA signs the certificate the box shows on port {{port}}. The box replaces the server certificate when it renews it or its address changes; the CA stays.
boxCert.self_signed: Import this certificate on the device as trusted, then send to port {{port}}.
boxCert.self_signedInfo: The box made this certificate itself, so a device does not trust it yet.
boxCert.issued: Import the certificates below on the device as trusted, then send to port {{port}}.
boxCert.issuedInfo: Another authority ({{issuer}}) issued the box certificate: the device must trust that authority. The file holds the certificates the box was given.
boxCert.fingerprint_issued: SHA-256 fingerprint of the first certificate
